extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research administrators, and institutions seeking DFG funding
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft's (DFG) funding portfolio and the principles for choosing and structuring funding instruments (individual vs institutional, thematic foci, career support, infrastructure). Useful for applicants and institutional planners deciding which DFG programme/instrument fits their needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between individual and institutional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinction is made between funding for individual researchers and funding for institutions, according to the requirements and objectives of the research to be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the type of funding instrument based on whether support is required for an individual researcher's project/career or for institutional capacities/structures. The page notes that individuals may also be nominated for research prizes, indicating separate pathways for personal recognition vs institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruments primarily designed to support research projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the DFG’s funding instruments are designed to support research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should treat the majority of DFG programmes as project-focused funding. These project instruments are organized into thematic/functional funding focuses (see grouping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of instruments into funding focuses (seven focuses + prizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: These instruments are grouped into seven funding focuses (an eighth funding focus encompasses prizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the funding-focus structure to identify appropriate instruments; the separate focus for prizes indicates distinct eligibility and purpose for award-type recognition versus project/institutional grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants centre on career development, research theme, or infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants centre on either research career development, or the research theme and the way in which it is addressed or the infrastructures required to address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting or designing proposals, identify whether the request is primarily for (a) advancing a researcher's career, (b) addressing a particular research theme/methodological approach, or (c) providing or improving research infrastructure — and align the application to that central aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with researchers' needs and disciplinary research approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities are aligned with the needs of researchers and are designed to reflect the research approaches used in the various academic research disciplines and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how the planned work matches disciplinary norms and methodological approaches and how the funding meets the actual needs of the researchers involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement and facilitation of diverse forms of cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: They also enable or facilitate diverse forms of cooperation between institutions, locations and disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG funding is intended to support collaborative work across institutional and disciplinary boundaries; proposals that clearly enable or facilitate cooperation (multi-institutional, cross-location, interdisciplinary) are consistent with this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional funding should enhance core academic and infrastructural areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding awarded to research institutions also helps to enhance their core areas and structures from an academic and infrastructural standpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution-level proposals should show how funding will strengthen the institution’s core research areas and infrastructure (both academic capacity and physical/organizational structures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research prizes as a distinct pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals can also be nominated for research prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prizes are treated separately (eighth funding focus) from project and institutional funding; nomination/eligibility and objectives differ from grant instruments and serve recognition purposes rather than project/infrastructure support.
